correctness.rationale: Every distance of distinct points lies in [1,2), hence the triangle inequality holds. Write each n uniquely as \(2^{k-1}(2q+1)\); assign sign \((-1)^q\) and magnitude \(r_n=1-2\alpha_n\). The exact pair identity \(d(n,m)-r_n-r_m=\alpha_{\min(n,m)}\) bounds slopes by the coefficient sup; divergent opposite-sign indices with fixed k realize each coefficient in the norm limit. Monotonicity gives \(\alpha_{\min(n,m)}\ge\alpha_n\) and d<2, proving the strict \((1-\alpha_n/2)\) local gap at every basepoint. The closed subspace follows from completeness of \(\ell_\infty\). Independent exact-rational checks evaluated 276 pair bounds on a 24-index sample, without replacing the all-sequence proof.
correctness.risk: The local gap varies by basepoint and vanishes in the limit; no uniform positive global gap follows.
